summary: ISO/IEC 42001 is the world's first international management system standard for artificial intelligence. It specifies requirements for establishing, implementing, maintaining, and continually improving an AI Management System (AIMS) within organizations. It provides a structured framework for managing AI-related risks and opportunities.

risk_tiers.description: AI applications where the organization's risk assessment identifies significant potential for adverse impacts on individuals, groups, or society. Requires comprehensive controls and enhanced management system processes.
criteria: AI system makes autonomous decisions with significant consequences
System processes sensitive personal data or biometric information
AI operates in safety-critical or life-affecting domains
Potential for significant financial, reputational, or legal impact
System affects fundamental rights or freedoms of individuals
AI system has broad societal impact or affects vulnerable groups

risk_tiers.description: AI applications with moderate risk levels where standard management system controls are appropriate. Regular monitoring and periodic review of risk assessments required.
criteria: AI system supports human decision-making with moderate impact
System processes non-sensitive data with appropriate safeguards
AI operates in commercial contexts with established oversight
Moderate potential for bias or fairness concerns
System has defined operational boundaries and constraints

risk_tiers.description: AI applications where risk assessment identifies minimal potential for adverse impacts. Basic management system controls and periodic review are sufficient.
criteria: AI system operates with full human oversight and control
System has negligible impact on individuals or society
AI used for internal optimization with no external effects

key_obligations.obligation: Establish an AI policy and AI management system with defined scope, leadership commitment, and allocated resources appropriate to the organization's context and AI risk profile
Conduct and maintain AI risk assessments identifying potential adverse impacts of AI systems, evaluating likelihood and severity, and determining appropriate risk treatment measures
Implement AI system impact assessments for affected individuals and groups, considering fairness, transparency, explainability, and potential for harm throughout the system lifecycle
Establish data management processes ensuring data quality, provenance, relevance, and appropriateness for AI system training, testing, and operation
key_obligations.article_reference: Annex A - Control A.7 Data for AI Systems

key_obligations.obligation: Implement transparency measures providing appropriate information about AI systems to stakeholders, including purpose, capabilities, limitations, and human oversight mechanisms
Monitor, measure, analyze, and evaluate AI system performance and the effectiveness of the AI management system, conducting internal audits and management reviews at planned intervals

enforcement_timeline: Published December 2023. Certification available through accredited certification bodies. Organizations can seek certification to demonstrate conformity. Complements but does not replace jurisdiction-specific AI regulations.
recent_changes: ISO/IEC 42001:2023 published as first AI management system standard
Certification bodies began offering ISO 42001 certification assessments
Supporting standards in development: ISO/IEC 42005 (AI impact assessment), ISO/IEC 42006 (certification body requirements)
